SHEIN
Built to last?
Ultra-fast fashion
Strategies for Sustainable Business
Professor Marc Francés · EADA Business School
· · · ·
October 2026

Good morning. Today we look at SHEIN, the ultra-fast-fashion giant. Our question is simple: is Shein's advantage built to last?

01 · Introduction
Who is Shein?
Base
China-based company
Founded in China. Parent company Roadget Business Pte. Ltd. registered in Singapore since 2021. Most production in Guangzhou, Guangdong.
Sells
Apparel, footwear, accessories, beauty and home goods
Model
Marketplace for third-party sellers
Brands
Shein, Sheglam, Dazy and Romwe
160markets

Shein describes itself as a global online fashion and lifestyle retailer. It was founded in China, and since 2021 its parent company, Roadget Business Pte. Ltd., has been registered in Singapore. But it still relies heavily on manufacturing in Guangzhou and Guangdong province, where most of its products are made and shipped from, although it also has suppliers and operations in Vietnam and other countries.

It sells apparel, footwear, accessories, beauty and home goods through its app and websites, and it also runs a marketplace for third-party sellers. Its brands include SHEIN, SHEGLAM, DAZY and ROMWE, and it operates in roughly 160 markets.

What Shein says
Mission

Values
Customers firstCelebrate diversityDrive results
What Shein faces
Controversy
Consumer and environmental claims
Labor claims
≠

While it is a very big company, there is a lot of controversy surrounding Shein. First, consumer and environmental claims: according to France, Shein misled customers with wrong price reductions and committed greenwashing. Second, labour claims, with reports of 75-hour work weeks and child labour cases.

Now compare that with what Shein says about itself. Its mission is making fashion accessible to all. Its values are putting customers first, celebrating diversity and driving results. Things that are far away from the claims made against them.

So how does Shein actually compete? {S2} will show you where its advantage really sits.

02 · Strategy levels
Strategy: Levels at Shein
Corporate (business you should be in)
From fashion retailer to platform: marketplace for other sellers, Hong Kong IPO, M&A (Missguided, Everlane), market exit and re-entry (India)
Business (tactics to beat competition)
Lowest prices, thousands of new items a day, app-first branding for Gen Z and influencers
Functional (focus on effectiveness)
Small test batches of 100 to 200 pieces, own software linking demand to suppliers, reorder only what sells
The real engine is at the bottom of the pyramid.

Strategy works at three levels. At the corporate level, the question is which business you should be in. Shein's answer keeps getting bigger: it is no longer only a fashion retailer but a platform, with a marketplace for other sellers, a listing in Hong Kong, and acquisitions like Missguided and Everlane. At the business level, the question is how to beat the competition: the lowest prices, thousands of new items every day, and an app built around Gen Z and influencers. But the real engine is at the functional level. Shein produces small test batches of 100 to 200 pieces, its own software connects customer demand directly to its suppliers, and it only reorders what sells.

02 · Concept clarification
Strategy: Concept clarification at Shein
01

Competitive advantage

Speed + price

02

Strategic positioning

Different activities from Zara or H&M: no factories, no stores, data decides what gets made

03

Operational effectiveness

Similar activities done faster and cheaper than rivals

Mostly operational effectiveness, and that can be copied.

So what kind of advantage does Shein have? It clearly has a competitive advantage: speed and price let it outperform its rivals. Part of it is real strategic positioning, because Shein performs different activities: it owns no factories and no stores, and data decides production. But most of its edge is operational effectiveness: doing similar activities better than rivals. And as Porter warns, operational effectiveness can be copied. Temu is already doing it, and in the first quarter of 2026 Shein posted a 99 million dollar loss as US tariffs hit. So the real question is whether this advantage is sustainable, which is what we look at next.

{S3} will now show you the engine behind Shein's growth.

03 · Growth drivers
Why did Shein grow so fast?
Source: Statista / ECDB, “Shein’s Meteoric Rise” (CC BY-ND). E-commerce net sales, US$ billion. *2024 forecast.
01Real-time demand sensing
Small test batches, then scale only the winners
02Agile supply chain
Responsive suppliers, fast restocking
03Digital-native customer acquisition
TikTok + influencers + “Shein hauls”
04Price advantage
Online only, direct to consumer, more variety for less

So which critical factors enabled Shein to grow? Look at this chart from Statista, based on ECDB estimates of e-commerce net sales. In 2018, shein.com sold 1.4 billion dollars online, less than zara.com at 2.1 billion and hm.com at 3.1 billion. By 2021 Shein had passed both, at 13.6 billion. And for 2024 the forecast was 48 billion dollars, while Zara and H&M stayed between 5 and 7 billion.

Four factors explain this rise. First, real-time demand sensing: Shein makes small test batches, then scales only the winners. Second, an agile supply chain, with responsive suppliers and fast restocking. Third, digital-native customer acquisition: TikTok, influencers and the famous "Shein hauls". Fourth, a price advantage: Shein is online only and sells direct to consumer, so it offers more variety for less.

03 · The functional engine, in motion
The Shein Flywheel
Advantage ≠ speed
It was the feedback loop between data, supply & demand.
Key message
Operational effectiveness ≠ sustainable competitive advantage

These factors feed each other in what we call the Shein flywheel. More data leads to better trend prediction. Better prediction means faster testing and fewer inventory bets. Fewer bets mean lower prices. Lower prices bring more customers, and more customers create more data. And the loop starts again.

So Shein's advantage is not just speed. It was the feedback loop between data, supply and demand. This is the operational effectiveness {S2} described at the bottom of the pyramid. And that is the key point: operational effectiveness is not the same as a sustainable competitive advantage.

A loop like this can be copied, and it can be slowed down. {S4} will show you what threatens it.

04 · Key threats and weaknesses
Threats
Outside the company
01
New environmental regulations or disclosure requirements
02
Financial sanctions against “ultra fast fashion”
03
Repercussions for ESG violations
04
Intense competition in the market

So what are Shein's key threats and weaknesses? Let's start with the threats, the forces outside the company.

First, new environmental regulations or disclosure requirements, which would force Shein to measure and report its real impact. Second, financial sanctions against "ultra fast fashion": lawmakers are now targeting exactly this business model. Third, repercussions for ESG violations: France has already fined Shein 40 million euros for misleading price reductions, and more cases like this could follow. And fourth, intense competition in the market: Temu and other platforms are copying the same ultra-cheap, app-first model, and they are fighting for exactly the same price-sensitive customers.

04 · Weaknesses, inside the company
7,667complaints to the Better Business Bureau in the last 3 years
Weaknesses
Extensive shipping times
Poor customer service capabilities ← 7,667
Disreputable brand image
Inconsistency in product quality
Encourages fast fashion and throwaway culture

Then the weaknesses, inside the company. Shipping times are extensive, and customer service capabilities are poor: Shein received 7,667 complaints to the Better Business Bureau in the last three years. Its brand image is disreputable, product quality is inconsistent, and it encourages fast fashion and a throwaway culture.

04 · Weaknesses
Unethical labor practices
75
hour work weeks
Severe underpayment
Exposure to toxic chemicals and PFAs

The heaviest weakness is unethical labor practices. Workers at supplier factories report 75-hour work weeks, severe underpayment, and exposure to toxic chemicals and PFAs. These claims come from investigations into Shein's supplier factories, and Shein disputes many of them. But they keep coming back, and they are the hidden cost behind the low price.

So with all these threats and weaknesses, is Shein's success built to last? {S5} will give you our answer.

05 · Is Shein’s success built to last?
Why it may last
01
Strong competitive advantage
Low prices, AI-assisted shopping, fast launches
02
Geographic expansion
India via Reliance Retail, Latin America, EU hubs
03
Business model diversification
Marketplace, supply-chain-as-a-service, Everlane
04
Adaptation to sustainability concerns
Reporting, circularity, ESG investment
05
Resilience despite scrutiny
Continued expansion, Hong Kong IPO

So, is Shein's success built to last? There are good reasons to think it may.

First, a strong competitive advantage: low prices, AI-assisted shopping, rapid trend forecasting and fast product launches continue to attract price-sensitive consumers. Second, geographic expansion: re-entering India through Reliance Retail, expanding in Mexico and Latin America, and establishing European logistics hubs help Shein diversify markets and strengthen distribution. Third, business model diversification: the marketplace model, supply-chain-as-a-service and the acquisition of Everlane expand revenue opportunities and position Shein beyond ultra-fast fashion. Fourth, adaptation to sustainability concerns: sustainability reporting, circularity initiatives and investment in ESG aim to address criticism and prepare for stricter regulations. And fifth, resilience despite scrutiny: continued expansion and progress toward a Hong Kong IPO suggest that Shein retains significant growth ambitions despite reputational and regulatory challenges.

05 · Risks to long-term success
What could break it
Tariffs
Fines
Labour concerns
Environmental criticism
Tighter ESG requirements
Could
increase costs and undermine its competitive advantage.

But there are real risks to long-term success. Tariffs, fines, labour concerns, environmental criticism and tighter ESG requirements could increase costs and undermine its competitive advantage. And remember: that advantage is low price.

Conclusion
Near term: likely to continue, supported by affordability, technology and international expansion.
However, its long-term success will depend on whether it can adapt to regulatory and sustainability pressures while maintaining its low-price advantage.

Our conclusion: Shein's success is likely to continue in the near term, supported by affordability, technology and international expansion. However, its long-term success will depend on whether it can adapt to regulatory and sustainability pressures while maintaining its low-price advantage.

Speed can be copied.
Built to last?
Near term: yes.
Long term: only if it adapts while keeping its low prices.
Thank you.

To sum up: Shein's speed and low prices drove its rise, but speed can be copied, and tariffs, fines and tighter ESG rules are already raising its costs. So is Shein built to last? In the near term, yes. In the long term, only if it adapts to regulatory and sustainability pressures while keeping its low-price advantage. Thank you.
